meta.title: The Classical World
meta.subtitle: From the Persian Wars to the rise of Islam: Europe, Africa, the Near East, Asia and the Americas, c. 500 BCE – 650 CE
meta.description: Empires and cultures of the classical and late antique world, from the Persian Wars and Warring States China to the fall of the Sasanians and the founding of Tang. It overlaps Ancient Civilizations from 500 to 330 BCE.
meta.credits: Dates and events come from English Wikipedia (read 17 November 2026) and the scholarly works it cites; each event lists its sources. Ancient dates are uncertain and scholars disagree. The lighter parts of a bar show the range of dates the cited sources give for its start and end, and the Dating menu re-plots a region under another dating system. Compiled with AI assistance and not yet reviewed by a specialist.

source.sourceLocation: lead ('as early as the 3rd century BCE')

events.title: Alexander the Great takes Tyre
events.descr: After a siege during which he builds a causeway to the island city. Eight thousand Tyrians die and 30,000 are sold into slavery.

events.title: Greco-Persian Wars
events.descr: From the Ionian Revolt to the end of hostilities; Persian invasions of Greece are repulsed in 492–490 and 480–479 BCE.

events.title: Alexander conquers the Achaemenid Empire
events.descr: The end of a Macedonian campaign that began in 336 BCE.

events.title: Warring States period
events.descr: Qin deposes the last Zhou king in 256 BCE and unifies China in 221 BCE.

events.title: La Venta Great Pyramid
events.descr: A radiocarbon date from Complex C, the great pyramid.

events.title: Earliest Maya writing
events.descr: The earliest inscriptions in an identifiably Maya script, in the Petén Basin.

events.title: Gauls defeat Rome at the Allia and sack the city
events.descr: Celts under Brennus defeat the Romans and sack Rome. The traditional (Varronian) date is 390 BCE; modern historians consider c. 387 the most probable.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox and Date of the battle

source.sourceLocation: Date of the battle (Polybius; most probable)

events.title: Latin League dissolved
events.descr: The league of Latin cities is dissolved.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.descr: The Persians are defeated in their first invasion of Greece.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.descr: A naval battle during Xerxes' invasion of Greece (481–479 BCE).

events.title: Peloponnesian War
events.descr: Athens and Sparta fight for hegemony over Greece; Persia backs Sparta from 413 and Athens surrenders in 404.

events.title: Reign of Philip II of Macedon
events.descr: King of Macedon from 359 BCE. He is assassinated in 336 and immediately succeeded by his son Alexander.

events.title: Philip II wins the Battle of Chaeronea
events.descr: The next year (337 BCE) Philip becomes hegemon of the Hellenic League.

events.title: Macedon moves its capital from Aigai to Pella
events.descr: Pella remains the capital until the kingdom ends in 168 BCE.

events.title: Samnite Wars
events.descr: Three wars (343–341, 327–304, 298–290 BCE) in which Rome subjugates the Samnites, despite their great victory at the Caudine Forks (321).

events.title: Teres I founds the Odrysian kingdom
events.descr: A Thracian kingdom founded after the failed Persian invasion of Greece. Philip II of Macedon conquers it in 340 BCE; Seuthes III revives it around 330.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.descr: The Greeks of Sicily defeat Hamilcar's expedition, crippling Carthage's power on the island for decades. Tradition put it on the same day as Salamis; modern scholars reject that.

events.title: Athenian expedition to Sicily
events.descr: Athens attacks Syracuse during the Peloponnesian War; the expedition is destroyed in 413 BCE.

events.title: Philip II defeats Ateas
events.descr: The Scythian king Ateas is killed in battle against Philip II of Macedon in Dobruja, and his empire falls to pieces.

events.title: Pazyryk burials
events.descr: Burials at Pazyryk and neighbouring sites in the Altai. A Saka (eastern Scythian) culture.

source.sourceLocation: Archaeology ('5th century BC'): start of century

events.title: Bantu speakers reach Lake Victoria and Angola
events.descr: The Western Stream reaches the southern edge of the rainforest and central Angola; the Eastern Stream, with Urewe pottery and one of the oldest iron-smelting centres in Africa, reaches west of Lake Victoria.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, Western Stream and Eastern Stream

events.title: Herodotus describes the Garamantes
events.descr: The earliest written record of them: "a very great nation" who herded cattle and farmed dates.

source.sourceLocation: History ('5th century BC'): start of century

events.title: Life of the Buddha
events.descr: He lives under Bimbisara and dies under Ajatashatru. Most scholars who give a date place his death within 20 years of 400 BCE; earlier scholarship used 563–483 BCE.

source.sourceLocation: infobox and Dating ('the earlier dates of 563–483 BCE')
infobox and Dating ('within 20 years either side of 400 BCE')

events.title: The Nanda dynasty takes Magadha
events.descr: The Nandas usurp the Shishunaga throne; Chandragupta Maurya overthrows them.

events.title: Sa Huỳnh–Kalanay trade network
events.descr: A trade sphere reaching Taiwan, southern Thailand, Borneo and the Philippines. The Sa Huỳnh, who buried their cremated dead in lidded jars, were most likely predecessors of the Austronesian-speaking Cham.

events.title: Metal tools in the Philippines
events.descr: Metal tools appear somewhere around 500 BC (Jocano: between 500 BC and 1 AD); other evidence points to iron in the ninth and tenth centuries BC.

source.sourceLocation: iron 'during the ninth and tenth centuries B.C.'

events.title: Kalanay Cave pottery
events.descr: Pottery dated 400 BC to AD 1500, similar to that of the Sa Huỳnh culture of southern Vietnam; iron and bronze artifacts were found at the site. It names the Sa Huỳnh–Kalanay interaction sphere, an Iron Age maritime trading network associated with the Austronesian peoples.

events.title: Buni culture in northern West Java
events.descr: A clay pottery culture on the coast of northern West Java, Jakarta and Banten, known for incised geometric decoration; burial gifts date from 400 BC to AD 100. The kingdom of Tarumanagara is probably its successor.

events.title: The kingdom of Lihyan at Dadan
events.descr: Most likely founded after Nabonidus arrived in north-west Arabia; it flourished for at least a century and a half. F. Winnett’s longer chronology places its beginning in the 6th century BC. The Gulf of Aqaba was called the Gulf of Lihyan.

events.title: Alexander the Great attacks the Getae
events.descr: On the lower Danube. Herodotus first used the name Getae; the Dacians were influenced by the Scythians and by the La Tène Celts who arrived in the 4th century BC.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, Name and Origins and ethnogenesis

events.title: Adena burial mounds
events.descr: Mounds built from hundreds of thousands of baskets of graded earth serve as burial and ceremonial sites; trade runs from Great Lakes copper to Gulf Coast shells. The Great Serpent Mound has been attributed to the culture, without conclusive evidence.

events.title: The Dorset culture begins
events.descr: They hunt seals from holes in the ice and make soapstone lamps (qulliq) burning seal oil; unlike earlier cultures they lack bow and arrow.

events.title: Monte Albán founded
events.descr: Built on a mountaintop in a previously uninhabited no-man’s-land; about 5,200 people live there by around 300 BCE. The Danzantes carvings date from its earliest period and show traits of Olmec culture.

events.title: Saladoid potters reach the Lesser Antilles and Puerto Rico
events.descr: Farmers and potters living in settled villages, believed to have spoken an Arawakan language; they displace the pre-ceramic Ortoiroid culture.

events.title: Nyatri Tsenpo, first Yarlung king (traditional date)
events.descr: Some Tibetan texts give 126 BC, others 414 BC. Tibetan texts name the kingdom of Zhangzhung (c. 500 BC–625 AD) as the precursor of later Tibetan kingdoms.

events.title: Battle of Thermopylae
events.descr: Greek city-states led by Sparta under Leonidas I hold the pass against Xerxes’ invasion; the Greeks defeat the invaders at Salamis later that year.

events.title: Pericles leads Athens
events.descr: The statesman and general of the Golden Age of Athens dies of the Plague of Athens in 429 BC.

events.title: The Parthenon built
events.descr: A temple on the Athenian Acropolis dedicated to Athena, begun when the Delian League was at the peak of its power; work on its decoration continued until 432 BC.

events.title: The trial and death of Socrates
events.descr: Athens tries the 70-year-old philosopher on two charges and he is put to death.

events.title: Plato founds the Academy
events.descr: Aristotle studies there for twenty years (367–347 BC); the school lasts until 83 BC.

events.title: Aristotle founds the Lyceum
events.descr: Returning to Athens after it fell under Macedonian rule, Aristotle sets up his school at the Lyceum.

events.title: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
events.descr: The tomb of Mausolus, built after his death in 353 BC; one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

events.title: Herodotus, historian of the Greco-Persian Wars
events.descr: A Greek historian and geographer from Halicarnassus; nothing in his Histories can be dated with certainty after 430 BC.

events.title: Mozi founds Mohism
events.descr: A philosophy emphasising universal love, social order, the will of Heaven, sharing and honouring the worthy.

events.title: The Hundred Schools of Thought
events.descr: Confucianism, Taoism, Mohism, Legalism and others flourish in the late Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods; their ideas profoundly influence East Asian culture.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, Confucianism, Taoism, Mohism and Legalism

events.title: Shang Yang’s reforms in Qin
events.descr: The reformer takes office in Qin in 359 BCE; his first reforms (356 BC) assign land by military merit and favour agriculture, and a second set follows in 350 BC.

events.title: Pāṇini’s Sanskrit grammar
events.descr: The ancient Sanskrit grammarian flourished in the mid 1st millennium BCE, variously dated between the 6th–5th and the 4th century BCE.

events.title: Death of Alexander the Great
events.descr: He dies at the age of 32, between the evenings of 10 and 11 June 323 BCE; fighting between his generals starts almost immediately.

events.title: Wars of the Diadochi
events.descr: Conflicts between Alexander’s generals over his empire. Ptolemy receives Egypt; after Corupedium (281 BC) Seleucus I is the last of the original successors, and Macedon is settled for the Antigonids only in 272 BC with the death of Pyrrhus.

events.title: Battle of Ipsus
events.descr: A coalition of Seleucus, Cassander and Lysimachus defeats Antigonus I, who is killed.

events.title: Seleucus takes Babylon: the Seleucid Empire
events.descr: After the battle of Gaza (312 BC), Seleucus captures the citadel of Babylon in August 311 BC. His empire is annexed by Rome under Pompey in 63 BC.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox, Rise of Seleucus and Babylonian War

events.title: Ptolemy I becomes pharaoh: the Ptolemaic Kingdom
events.descr: Ptolemy, who had ruled Egypt as satrap since 323 BC, takes the title of basileus and pharaoh. The kingdom lasts until the death of Cleopatra VII in 30 BC.

events.title: The Library of Alexandria
events.descr: Probably built under Ptolemy II Philadelphus (285–246 BC), though Ptolemy I may have planned it. Its decline begins with a purge of intellectuals in 145 BC; part is burned by Julius Caesar in 48 BC.

events.title: The Greco-Bactrian Kingdom breaks away
events.descr: Founded by the Seleucid satrap Diodotus I; it falls around 120 BC as the Parthians and nomads such as the Saka and Yuezhi press in. The Yuezhi later found the Kushan Empire.

events.title: Archimedes killed at the siege of Syracuse
events.descr: One of the greatest mathematicians of all time (c. 287 – c. 212 BC), he designed war machines to defend Syracuse and was killed by a Roman soldier.

events.title: The Rosetta Stone decree
events.descr: A decree issued at Memphis on behalf of Ptolemy V Epiphanes on 27 March 196 BC.

events.title: Battle of Pydna: Rome ends the Antigonid kingdom
events.descr: Defeat in the Third Macedonian War ends the dynasty that had ruled much of Hellenistic Greece since 294 BC.

events.title: Attalus III leaves Pergamon to Rome
events.descr: The childless king bequeaths his realm to the Roman Republic; after a revolt it becomes the Roman province of Asia (129 BC).

events.title: First Punic War
events.descr: It breaks out on Sicily and lasts twenty-three years, until Carthage is defeated.

events.title: Second Punic War: Hannibal
events.descr: Hannibal is defeated at Zama in 202 BC and a treaty follows in 201 BC.

events.title: Rome destroys Carthage
events.descr: Rome declares war in 149 BC and storms Carthage in 146 BC; its territory becomes the Roman province of Africa.

events.title: Battle of Carrhae: Parthia defeats Crassus
events.descr: Fought between the Roman Republic and the Parthian Empire; Cicero called the war "nulla causa", since Parthia had a treaty with Rome.

events.title: Julius Caesar assassinated
events.descr: Killed on the Ides of March (15 March), three days before he was to leave on a campaign against the Parthians; the Liberators’ civil war follows (43–42 BC).

events.title: Battle of Actium
events.descr: On 2 September 31 BC Octavian’s fleet under Agrippa defeats Antony and Cleopatra. Cleopatra takes her life on 12 August 30 BC, ending the Ptolemaic Kingdom and the Hellenistic period, and Egypt becomes a Roman province.

events.title: Octavian becomes Augustus: the Roman Empire
events.descr: The Senate grants Octavian the title Augustus on 16 January 27 BC, often seen as the end of the Republic. He rules as the first emperor until his death in AD 14 and makes peace with Parthia and Kush.

events.title: The Roman Empire at its greatest extent
events.descr: At the time of Trajan’s death (r. 98–117 AD) the empire covers some 5,000,000 km².

events.title: Crisis of the Third Century
events.descr: It begins with the assassination of Severus Alexander by his own troops; by 268 the empire has split into three competing states, and Aurelian (270–275) turns the tide.

events.title: The Tetrarchy
events.descr: Diocletian divides imperial rule between two augusti and two caesares; Constantine’s victory at the Milvian Bridge (312) begins its end.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.descr: The 13 February 313 agreement to treat Christians benevolently; Christianity becomes the state religion with the Edict of Thessalonica in 380.

events.title: Constantinople becomes the capital
events.descr: Founded in 324 on the site of Byzantium and dedicated on 11 May 330 as the new eastern capital of the Roman Empire.

events.title: Battle of Adrianople
events.descr: In 376 the Huns had driven many Goths into the empire; at Adrianople they defeat the Romans.

events.title: Death of Theodosius I: East and West divide
events.descr: He dies after making Christianity the state religion, ending the unified empire (27 BC – AD 395).

sources.sourceLocation: infobox and Transition to late antiquity

events.title: The Visigoths sack Rome
events.descr: On 24 August 410 Alaric’s Visigoths enter Rome and pillage it for three days. The Vandals sack it again in 455.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox, lead, Third siege and sack, and Aftermath

events.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.descr: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last Western emperor, and sends the imperial insignia to the Eastern emperor Zeno.

sources.sourceLocation: lead and Fall in the West

events.title: Reign of Justinian I
events.descr: He rewrites Roman law as the Corpus Juris Civilis (final code 534) and retakes North Africa from the Vandals (533–534) and Italy from the Ostrogoths; the empire reaches its zenith in 555.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox, Life, Legislative activities, Conquest of North Africa, War in Italy and Results

events.title: Hagia Sophia built
events.descr: Justinian’s basilica rises after the second church burns in the Nika riots of January 532; it is inaugurated on 27 December 537.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox and Church of Justinian I

events.title: The Plague of Justinian
events.descr: It reaches Roman Egypt in 541 and every corner of the empire by 543; Justinian catches it and recovers. It strikes the Sasanian Empire too and recurs until the mid-8th century.

events.title: The Parthian Empire
events.descr: Centred in ancient Iran; Mithridates I (r. c. 171–132 BC) greatly expands it by seizing Media and Mesopotamia from the Seleucids.

events.title: The Maccabean Revolt
events.descr: A revolt against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV’s repression of Judaism. The Maccabees take Jerusalem in 164 BCE; Judas Maccabeus dies in 160, and in 141 Simon Thassi expels the Greeks. An alliance with Rome helps secure independence.

events.title: Herod the Great rules Judea
events.descr: A Roman client king; after his death the Romans divide his kingdom among his heirs. Some scholars (Steinmann) date his reign 36–1 BCE.

events.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
events.descr: In Jerusalem, in the Roman province of Judaea; dated AD 30 or 33.

events.title: Rome destroys Jerusalem and the Second Temple
events.descr: The decisive event of the First Jewish Revolt (66–73 CE): the siege runs from 13 April to 8 September 70.

events.title: The Bar Kokhba revolt
events.descr: Sparked by Hadrian’s plan to rebuild Jerusalem as Aelia Capitolina; the rebels hold an independent state for over three years until Betar falls in 135. The province is renamed Syria Palaestina.

events.title: Rome annexes the Nabataean Kingdom
events.descr: Independent since the mid-3rd century BC, it becomes the province of Arabia Petraea.

events.title: The Sasanian Empire
events.descr: Ardashir I defeats the Parthians at the Battle of Hormozdgan on 28 April 224; the last pre-Islamic Iranian empire rules from Ctesiphon until 651.

events.title: Shapur I defeats Rome at Edessa
events.descr: A disastrous Roman defeat; the same year Odaenathus of Palmyra defeats Shapur near the Euphrates.

events.title: Zenobia’s Palmyrene Empire
events.descr: In 270 Zenobia rapidly conquers most of the Roman east, including Egypt; in 271 she claims the imperial title. Aurelian besieges Palmyra in 272 and razes it after a revolt in 273.

events.title: Armenia adopts Christianity
events.descr: The traditional date; scholars propose dates from 284 to no later than 325, and many favour 314.

events.title: Aksum conquers Himyar
events.descr: After the conquest Christianity becomes Himyar’s main religion; Sasanian intervention brings Yemen under Persian influence in 575 or 578.

events.title: The last Roman–Persian war
events.descr: The Sasanians conquer much of the Levant, parts of Anatolia and, for the first time, Egypt; they take Jerusalem after a three-week siege in 614. Heraclius strikes back from 622, the Persians fail before Constantinople in 626, and Persia, torn by civil war, seeks peace.

events.title: The Hijrah: start of the Islamic calendar
events.descr: Its date equates to 16 July 622; the year is the epoch of the Islamic calendar.

events.title: Battle of the Yarmuk
events.descr: On 15–20 August 636 the Rashidun Caliphate defeats the Byzantine army; Byzantine Syria is annexed.

events.title: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
events.descr: The second Rashidun invasion of Sasanian territory wins a decisive victory (16–19 November 636).

events.title: Fall of the Sasanian Empire
events.descr: By 651 most cities of the Iranian lands are in Muslim hands; the Rashidun Caliphate annexes the empire.

events.title: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Maurya Empire
events.descr: His conquest of Magadha is generally dated to c. 322–319 BCE; an alternative chronology places these events in c. 311–305 BCE. He reigns until c. 297 BCE.

events.title: Seleucid–Mauryan war
events.descr: Fought sometime between 305 and 303 BCE between Chandragupta and Seleucus I Nicator; it ends in a marriage alliance.

events.title: Reign of Ashoka
events.descr: Mauryan emperor from c. 268 BCE until his death in 232 BCE. His edicts, inscriptions of the 3rd century BCE, are read again only after the decipherment of the Brahmi script in the 19th century.

events.title: Kalinga War
events.descr: Ashoka conquers Kalinga in the eighth year of his reign, according to his own edicts. The war began an era of more than 40 years of relative peace.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox, Course of the war and Aftermath

source.sourceLocation: infobox and Course of the war

events.title: Buddhism reaches Sri Lanka
events.descr: Theravada Buddhism is introduced during the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa.

events.title: Pushyamitra Shunga kills the last Maurya
events.descr: The assassination of Brihadratha by Pushyamitra Shunga ends the Maurya Empire and begins the Shunga Empire.

events.title: Demetrius I invades India: the Indo-Greek Kingdom
events.descr: The Graeco-Bactrian king Demetrius I invades India from Bactria. The Indo-Greeks disappear as a political entity around 10 AD.

events.title: Menander I
events.descr: Indo-Greek king; the precise dates of his reign remain elusive. Patanjali’s Mahabhashya, around 150 BC, describes a failed campaign of Menander as far as Mathura. According to tradition, he embraced the Buddhist faith.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox, lead, Reign and Menander and Buddhism

events.title: Maues, the first Saka king in India
events.descr: The first rulers of the Indo-Scythian kingdom are Maues (c. 85–60 BCE) and Vonones (c. 75–65 BCE).

events.title: Kujula Kadphises unites the Yuezhi: the Kushan Empire
events.descr: Kujula Kadphises (25–85), the first ruler, unites the Yuezhi tribes into a confederation. The Kushan Empire fragments into semi-independent kingdoms in the 3rd century AD.

events.title: A Kushan army fights Ban Chao near Khotan
events.descr: Ban Chao fights battles near Khotan with a Kushan army of 70,000 men.

sources.sourceLocation: Conquests in India and Central Asia

events.title: Reign of Kanishka
events.descr: The empire reaches its zenith. Around 127 CE he replaces Greek with Bactrian as the official language of administration. He never converts to Buddhism but gives it royal sponsorship, and heads the 4th Buddhist Council in Kashmir. Earlier scholars dated his accession to 78 CE.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox and Kanishka and Buddhism

events.title: Naneghat inscription of Satakarni I
events.descr: Dated to 70–60 BCE, in the reign of Satakarni I.

events.title: The Pallavas become a major southern power
events.descr: During the reigns of Mahendravarman I (600–630) and Narasimhavarman I (630–668).

events.title: Kashyapa I rules from Sigiriya
events.descr: Kashyapa I (473–491) chooses Sigiriya to be his capital.

events.title: Coronation of Chandragupta I
events.descr: Crowned on 26 February 320. The Gupta Empire, established c. 240, exists from the mid 3rd century to the mid 6th century CE.

events.title: Reign of Samudragupta
events.descr: The second Gupta emperor. Modern scholars variously assign the start of his reign from c. 319 CE to c. 350 CE.

events.title: Reign of Chandragupta II
events.descr: Gupta emperor until his death in c. 415. The beginning of his reign can be dated to either 376–377 CE or 380–381 CE.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox and Period of reign

events.title: Chandragupta II defeats the last Western Satrap
events.descr: Rudrasimha III, the last of the Western Satraps, is defeated by the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II.

events.title: Nalanda founded
events.descr: Established by the Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I; it operates for almost a thousand years, until around 1400 CE.

events.title: Gupta–Hunnic Wars
events.descr: Wars between the Gupta Empire and the Huns; the Alchon Huns invade India between the 4th and 6th centuries CE.

events.title: Ajanta Caves: the second phase
events.descr: Buddhist cave monuments dating from the second century BCE to about 480 CE. The second phase falls in a brief period of 460–480 CE according to later scholarship (400–650 CE in older accounts), circa 480 CE under King Harishena.

events.title: Aryabhata
events.descr: Mathematician-astronomer of the Gupta era. He states he was 23 years old in 3600 Kali Yuga, 499 CE. His Aryabhatiya is translated into Arabic c. 820 CE.

events.title: Harsha, emperor of Kannauj
events.descr: Crowned at an assembly in April 606, after the downfall of the Gupta Empire in the middle of the 6th century; he rules until his death in 647. An invasion he leads is repelled on the banks of the Narmada in the winter of 618–619.

sources.sourceLocation: lead, infobox, Early years and Reign

events.title: Tang Taizong sends Wang Xuance to India
events.descr: The Tang Chinese emperor Tang Taizong sends Wang Xuance to India.
